finding: The 120 sf exemption comes from California Building Code 105.2, as reproduced in San Francisco's code, and covers only one-story detached storage sheds.

quote: One-story detached accessory buildings or structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses, and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet (11.15 m2).

finding: Los Angeles County's commercial plan-review checklist says mezzanine floor area must be counted in the story it sits in, so a mezzanine adds to building area under plan check.
source_title: NON-RESIDENTIAL Plan Review (2023 Code) - County of Los Angeles
quote: Mezzanine floor area must be included in the story in which it is located.

finding: Under California Health and Safety Code §19955.3, a mezzanine larger than one-third of the room's floor area counts as an additional story, and it needs at least 7 feet of clear height above and below.
source_title: California Health and Safety Code § 19955.3
quote: When the total area of any "mezzanine floor" exceeds 33 1/3 percent of the total floor area in that room, it shall be considered as constituting an additional "story." The clear height above and below a "mezzanine floor" construction shall be not less than seven feet.

finding: San Diego County's commercial plan-check list applies the CBC 505 limit that mezzanines may not exceed one-third of the room's floor area, which confirms they go through building plan review.
source_title: Commercial Building Code Plan Check (PDS 492) - San Diego County
quote: Aggregate area of mezzanine(s) shall not exceed one-third the floor area of the room or space in which the mezzanine is located
